newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline demand emerges.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline demand emerges.

text.p: Gasoline fell amid aggressive offers, and the emergence of a buyer in the Singapore market and demand into Australia and Saudi Arabia are not likely to prop up the market, traders said on Tuesday.

Offers for the 95-octane unleaded grade dropped to as low as $25.80 per barrel fob Singapore, from $26.35 on Monday, but a Dutch trader finally emerged to buy the April 23-27 lifting cargo of 50,000 barrels at that level.
"It won't support the market," said one trader. "It is only a top-up piece."
Mobil is seeking one million barrels each for May and June delivery into Australia during its two refineries' maintenance shutdown in May, sources said.
But bearish traders said the grade being sought - 93 RON, 82 MON - was very difficult to make.
Traders also said Saudi Aramco issued a tender to buy up to 300,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for prompt delivery in April/May. But the tender which closes April 9 is a closed one.

On the supply side, Thai refiner Rayong Refinery Company Limited offered to sell around 230,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline lifting April 17 in a tender closing April 8 and valid on the same day, industry sources said.
Vietnam awarded its second quarter tender for gasoline, but all six 18,000-tonne cargoes of 83-octane gasoline with lead content of 0.15 grammes per litre will originate from Russia.

Daxin Petroleum Pte Ltd, Japan's Mitsui and Kuo International each are to supply two cargoes at a premium of 80 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City, Danang or Hongai.
The source said offers of non-Russian gasoline were made at between $2.00 and $2.50 per barrel above Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis.
Vietnam bought five 17,000-tonne cargoes of Russian origin for the first quarter at a premium of 50 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis.
Naphtha swaps firmed slightly with May last quoted at $21.55/$21.65 per barrel, up 40 cents from Monday.

But sentiment was still bearish with state-owned Indian Oil Corp's tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) awarded to Dutch trader Vitol at $25.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob Vizag on the east coast, compared to its last LAN award at a $17.00 discount for a cargo lifting March 30-April 1.
The tender for the cargo lifting mid-April closed on April 3 and was valid until April 4.
In a tender which closed at the same time, IOC has sold 30,000 tonnes of LAN to Japanese trader Itochu at $18.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob Bombay on the west coast lifting mid-April.
IOC's last LAN cargo from Bombay lifting February 20-22 was awarded at $23.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob.
IOC issued two new tenders, offering 25,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) and 27,000 tonnes of LAN from Madras, both lifting April 21-25 from Bombay
Both tenders close April 10 and bids should be valid for one day.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
